papers.title_in_file: A quantum algorithm for learning a graph of bounded degree
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, statements of Theorems 1.1 to 1.3, concluding remarks; proofs in sections 3 and 4 skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that gives a quantum algorithm learning the edge set of a bounded-degree graph with few quantum OR queries.

assertions.value: The paper proves that for a graph with maximum degree d there is a quantum algorithm that identifies all m edges using quantum OR queries, with the query count given in the theorem statement, and that the algorithm succeeds with high probability.
quotes: Let G be a graph on n vertices with m unknown edges and maximum degree d. Then there is a quantum algorithm that identifies all m edges in G using at most
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem in section 1, proved in section 4
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says the query count matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors when the maximum degree is bounded; the exact bound is in a formula the text extraction garbles.

assertions.value: The authors define the setting as an OR-query model: a set S of vertices is submitted to an oracle, which says whether S induces at least one edge, and quantum queries may be made in superposition.
quotes: induces at least one edge in G.
Here we consider a more general model, where we may query an arbitrary subset of vertices
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the query model, abstract and section 1
assertions.reader_inference: The result is a query-count result in an oracle model, not a runtime on hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that for a graph made of two cliques joined by arbitrary edges, which has large maximum degree, their algorithm performs optimally up to logarithmic factors.
quotes: our algorithm performs optimally, up to logarithmic factors
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5 states the case in which the bound is tight
assertions.reader_inference: The text says the algorithm beats the earlier Montanaro and Shao bound only when the maximum degree is small relative to the square root of m.

papers.title_in_file: Level Generation with Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.what_it_is: An applied study that uses a quantum reservoir computing model, run in simulation, to generate Super Mario Bros and Roblox game levels.

assertions.value: The authors report that in noiseless simulation on one Super Mario Bros level the error rate of broken transitions stays below 5% for temperatures as high as T = 2, where originality for sequences of length 2 and 3 exceeds and matches, respectively, that of the Markov generator.
quotes: Notably, the error rate remains low (below 5%) for temperatures as high as T = 2 where the originality for sequences of length 2 and 3 exceeds and matches, respectively, that of the Markov generator.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study on a single training level
assertions.reader_inference: Only one training level (level 1-2) is used, and the comparison is against a simple Markov chain, not a stronger classical generative model.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a Roblox obstacle course the QRC significantly outperforms the Markov chain generator, with an error rate as low as 36% for the optimal number of 6 qubits.
quotes: Our results indicate that QRC significantly outperforms the Markov chain generator, achieving an error rate as low as 36% for the optimal number of 6 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study on a hand-designed course
assertions.reader_inference: An error rate of 36% on the long critical sequence is high for a playable game; the paper itself notes errors must be corrected afterwards.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation a depolarization rate of 1% significantly diminishes the QRC's ability to replicate sequences longer than 15 features, and that the theoretical advantage of adding noise does not translate to better level generation.
quotes: Even a small depolarization rate of 1% significantly diminishes the QRC's ability to replicate sequences longer than 15 features.
the theoretical advantage in adding noise [18] does not translate to better level generation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from noise simulation, one level
assertions.reader_inference: Current hardware is described in the paper as operating near 3% depolarization, above the level that already hurts the model.

assertions.value: The authors state that results come from classical simulation of the quantum circuit, and that a full hardware implementation is beyond the scope of this work.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.1 and Section III.B, p.4
quotes: we resort to simulating the quantum circuit on non-quantum computers and leave the training and generation on real quantum hardware for later works.
the development and discussion of a full hardware implementation is beyond the scope of this work.
assertions.certainty_reason: Introduction p.1 and Section III.B p.4 state the limit
assertions.reader_inference: No result in the paper was produced on quantum hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search framework for combinatorial optimization problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 2 overview, benchmark discussion and conclusion; TSP implementation details skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid algorithm, AtomTreeSearch, that embeds a neutral-atom quantum sampling subroutine, emulated classically, in Monte Carlo Tree Search and benchmarks it on the Traveling Salesman Problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that on random Euclidean instances with up to 60 cities and TSPLIB instances with up to 100 cities, their hybrid algorithm generally matches or outperforms both OR-Tools and simulated annealing.
quotes: instances of up to 60 cities on random Euclidean instances and up to 100 cities on TSPLIB instances.
Our hybrid algorithm generally matches or outperforms both OR-Tools and simulated annealing on these instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark from one study, with emulated quantum subroutine
assertions.reader_inference: The instances are small; the comparison is against a general-purpose solver and a simulated annealing baseline, and the quantum step was not run on quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum subroutine produces more diverse and higher-quality branches than the classical alternative subroutines they compared.
quotes: we find that the quantum subroutine produces more diverse and higher-quality branches compared to classical alternate subroutines.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study with an emulated subroutine
assertions.reader_inference: The 'quantum' branches come from a classical emulation of the neutral-atom device, so the result shows a property of the sampling distribution, not a hardware advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum evolution is emulated using classical simulation tools, that the simulations are limited, and that they cannot emulate the quantum protocol at a larger scale.
assertions.anchor: Section 2.4 and Section 5, p.8 and p.22
quotes: is emulated using classical simulation tools such as
under limited computational resources due to our inability to emulate our quantum protocol at a larger scale.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 2.4 and Section 5 state the emulation limit
assertions.reader_inference: Claims about advantage on real neutral-atom hardware are untested in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: A Review on Quantum Circuit Optimization using ZX-Calculus
papers.version_note: File is arXiv v6, dated 28 Mar 2026; the record year is 2026 and the file name says 2025.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, background overview and the Challenges section; the technique-by-technique survey sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of ZX-calculus methods for optimizing quantum circuits, classified by technique, target metric and hardware architecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that they review ZX-based optimization of quantum circuits, categorized by optimization technique, target metric and intended quantum computing architecture.
quotes: We review ZX-based optimization of quantum circuits, categorizing them by optimization techniques, target metrics and intended quantum computing architecture.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the scope of the survey

assertions.value: The authors state that circuit extraction from ZX-diagrams is computationally expensive, and that the extraction algorithm determines the characteristics of the resulting quantum circuit.
quotes: Circuit extraction from ZX-diagrams is computationally expensive, and the specified extraction algorithm determines the characteristics of the resulting quantum circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey statement of background results attributed to other work

assertions.value: The authors state that the computational complexity of rule-based rewriting of ZX-diagrams grows rapidly with diagram size, which limits existing techniques to small-scale quantum circuits.
quotes: With an increase in size of ZXdiagrams, the computational complexity grows rapidly, limiting the practical application of existing techniques to small-scale quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey author's statement about the field, no single study behind it
assertions.reader_inference: The same section proposes reinforcement learning as a route to heuristics, so it touches ML for compilation, but only as a future direction.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum circuit for exponentiation of Hamiltonians: an algorithmic description based on tensor products
papers.what_it_is: A short methods paper that gives an algorithm to build the quantum circuit for the exponential of a tensor product of Pauli operators.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate a straightforward and efficient method to construct compact circuits for Pauli-string exponentials that are easy to implement.
quotes: We demonstrate a straightforward and efficient method to construct compact circuits that are easy to implement.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; the text gives no gate-count or depth comparison
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not report gate counts or depth against other constructions.

assertions.value: The authors report that experimental results confirm the correctness of the algorithm, and that the circuit it gives for an example matches the circuit generated by the Qiskit library.
quotes: Experimental results confirm its correctness in defining quantum circuits aligned with the Qiskit library's results.
gives a quantum circuit that meets the quantum circuit generated by application of algorithm 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: Agreement shown on a small example against one library
assertions.reader_inference: The check is one example compared with Qiskit's decomposition, not a general verification.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work aims to make the concept more accessible to computer scientists, with an algorithmic perspective rather than a purely mathematical one.
quotes: this work aims to make the concept more accessible to computer scientists, offering an algorithmic perspective rather than a purely mathematical one
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion states the paper's aim and scope
assertions.reader_inference: The paper is an exposition of a construction, not a new resource-reduction result.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Feature Selection with Higher-Order Binary Optimization on Trapped-Ion Hardware
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper by Kipu Quantum and IonQ authors that runs a higher-order binary optimization formulation of feature selection on IonQ Forte hardware and compares it with classical baselines on two datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report good qualitative agreement between hardware executions and noiseless simulations, and state that this supports the feasibility of implementing higher-order feature-selection Hamiltonians on current trapped-ion processors.
quotes: The results show good qualitative agreement between hardware executions and noiseless simulations, supporting the feasibility of implementing higher-order featureselection Hamiltonians on current trapped-ion processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on two datasets
assertions.reader_inference: The agreement is described as qualitative; the paper also notes discrepancies for features near the selection threshold.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Gallstone dataset the IonQ Forte solution, reducing dimensionality from 32 to 19 features, outperforms both PCA with 95% explained variance and SelectKBest based on mutual information.
quotes: the IonQ Forte solution (reducing dimensionality from 32 to 19 features) outperforms both PCA (with 95% explained variance) and the SelectKBest method based on mutual information.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one small dataset; metric values are in Table I
assertions.reader_inference: Table I holds the metric values and was not quoted. The Gallstone dataset is small, and the text reports no repeated runs or confidence intervals. The authors are affiliated with the quantum vendors involved.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Spambase dataset the quantum-selected subset reduces dimensionality from 32 to 23 features while maintaining classification performance compared to using all features.
quotes: the quantum-selected subset reduces the dimensionality from 32 to 23 features while maintaining
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from hardware runs on one dataset
assertions.reader_inference: Table II holds the metric values and was not quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because of the 32-qubit hardware limit, each dataset was preselected to 32 features before the quantum step.
quotes: Due to the 32-qubit hardware limit, each dataset was preselected to 32 features
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV states the hardware limit and the preselection step
assertions.reader_inference: A classical mutual-information ranking does the first reduction, so the quantum step only chooses among the 32 pre-ranked features.

papers.title_in_file: Uma Introducao ao Variational Quantum Eigensolver Aplicado a Quimica (Portuguese body text; English abstract)
papers.version_note: The body text is in Portuguese; the file carries an English abstract and matches the record's English title. Quotes below are from the Portuguese body or the English abstract.
papers.partial_detail: English abstract, Portuguese introduction, the complexity discussion in section 5 and the conclusion; chemistry background sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A tutorial review of VQE applied to molecular simulation, with a complexity analysis of the algorithm for a simple case.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given the current limits of quantum computers, variational quantum algorithms, especially VQE, stand out as a feasible approach to demonstrating advantages over classical methods in the near term.
quotes: stand out as a feasible approach to demonstrating advantages over classical methods in the near term.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim about the field with no study behind it in this paper
assertions.reader_inference: The introduction says it is not clear from the literature whether VQE has any advantage over the best classical algorithms, so the abstract claim is a hope, not a finding.

assertions.value: The authors derive, for the simplest version of the algorithm, a circuit depth that grows as O(kN 3) in the best case and a total scaling governed by a term of order N 7, and state that this makes VQE hard to run on NISQ computers.
quotes: a profundidade do circuito crescendo com O(kN 3) faz com que mesmo circuitos com algumas dezenas
a escalabilidade total regida por um termo de ordem N 7 poderia deixar o
assertions.certainty_reason: Operation-count derivation for a didactic simple case, not a proved bound or a run
assertions.reader_inference: The text says better circuits and fewer-measurement methods exist that may lower these costs, so the scaling is for the simplest version.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main difficulty for VQE lies in the Barren plateau problem.
quotes: a maior dificuldade se localiza no Barren plateau
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about the field, supported by cited work
assertions.reader_inference: The same passage cites work arguing that many Barren-plateau-free variational circuits can be simulated classically.

papers.title_in_file: Scalable Quantum Algorithms for Noisy Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, chapter summaries and introductions of chapters 2 to 7, the end of chapter 7 and the full Conclusion (chapter 8); derivations and appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: A doctoral thesis that develops stochastic and dual-formulation methods to cut the measurement cost of variational quantum algorithms for ground-state preparation and time evolution.

assertions.value: The authors report that, combined with error mitigation, the stochastic algorithm is scaled up to 27 qubits on hardware, a regime they describe as challenging for variational quantum algorithms on noisy computers without their algorithms.
quotes: In combination with error mitigation techniques, the latter is scaled up to 27 qubits; into a regime that variational quantum algorithms are challenging to scale to on noisy quantum computers without our algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result for one model, from one thesis
assertions.reader_inference: The 27-qubit run is an imaginary-time evolution of a hardware-native Ising model, chosen to fit the chip.

assertions.value: The author states that an unbiased estimator of the quantum geometric tensor constructs samples at a constant cost, instead of a cost that scales quadratically with the number of parameters in the ansatz circuit.
quotes: we introduce an unbiased estimator of the QGT which allows to construct samples at a constant cost instead of scaling quadratically with the number of parameters in the variational ansatz circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Taken from the conclusion; the derivation in chapters 5 and 6 was not read in full
assertions.reader_inference: The coordinator may raise this to high after reading the proof in chapter 5.

assertions.value: The author reports that, with a suitable initialization, the dual formulation requires asymptotically fewer measurements in numerical benchmarks than the approach based on the quantum geometric tensor.
quotes: In combination with a suitable initialization, we observe that this approach requires asymptotically less measurements in numerical benchmarks than the QGT-based approach to time evolution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from numerical benchmarks, supported by sampling-complexity bounds
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis says bounds on the sampling complexity further support this.

assertions.value: The author states that a potential drawback of DualQTE is that it relies on an accurate evaluation of the fidelity, which can be costly to evaluate on near-term devices.
quotes: A potential drawback of DualQTE is that it relies on an accurate evaluation of the fidelity, which can be costly to evaluate on near-term devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7.4 states the limit of the method
